page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity storage and memory-optimized server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core.

The instance is provisioned with a massive 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which accelerate cryptographic and vector-based operations.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached small-block reads reaching 7,287.47 GB/sec. Large-block uncached reads and writes fall into the strong top 25% category at 229.38 GB/sec and 140.83 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance, handling 122.77 million operations per second for Redis. Large language model inference shows top-tier prompt processing speeds for small models, though text generation for larger models scales down to average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L96as_v4 offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a substantial memory footprint, making it highly effective for data-intensive workloads without the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware. This hardware profile is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput data warehousing, software build systems, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
